title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)' Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic framework for tame-topological 'atlases'. The data are: a set M of 'figures' (multiplicités), ordered by inclusion ≤, with intersections X∩Y; a distinguished subset L of 'lieux', which play the role of point-like or cell-like atoms; a disjointness relation ∥; and a further relation written ⋔ / ≭, discussed below. For a figure X, omb(X) (the 'ombre', or shadow, of X) is the set of lieux attached to X. An atlas is 'ensembliste' when M ⊂ Figel(L), i.e. figures are realised as sets of lieux.

Axioms from the previous page.
- At 9 (criterion of disjunction by lieux): if every lieu of X is disjoint from every lieu of Y, then X ∥ Y.
- Atens 2 (set-theoretic case): distinct lieux are disjoint.

Corollary 1. Assume At 9 and Atens 2. Then for figures F, G: F ∥ G iff x ∥ y for all x ∈ omb(F), y ∈ omb(G).
- Sufficiency is At 9.
- Necessity uses the (presumably earlier) heredity of disjointness to subfigures.
- Combined with Atens 2, and assuming no lieu is disjoint from itself, this says F ∥ G iff omb(F) ∩ omb(G) = ∅. Disjointness is then read off from shadows.
- For general (non-set-theoretic) atlases he notes that one finds something else.

Corollary 2. Formula (1.58), not visible here, holds whenever F satisfies At 9.

Optional axiom At 9'. Let X, Y ∈ M and F = X∩Y, taken in F̃, one of the auxiliary structures. Suppose every lieu x of X not in omb(F) and every lieu y of Y not in omb(F) satisfy x ∥ y; hence x ≠ y. This implies omb(X) ∩ omb(Y) = omb(F). He draws this as a little diagram: omb(X) and omb(Y) both pointing to omb(F). The conclusion is X ⋔ Y.
- By the next page, (1.59), the relation ⋔/≭ restricted to lieux satisfies x ∥ y ⟺ (x ≭ y and x ≠ y). On lieux it therefore means 'equal or disjoint', which is a clean or compatible intersection.
- So X ⋔ Y should be read as 'X and Y are in good (transverse/compatible) position': they meet exactly along their common part F, like two closed cells of a regular complex meeting in a common subcomplex, or two strata/semialgebraic sets whose union is the gluing along F.
- In words: if the shadows overlap only along the shadow of the intersection, the figures are compatible.
- NB: the converse would follow from an 'axiome de disposition' given later (p.72).
- Grothendieck comments that the axiom expresses a ⋔-compatibility of the 'primitive multistructures'.

Next page. He weighs putting all the weight on the single relation ≭ on L (an atlas described set-theoretically from one relation). He observes this fails in the most interesting examples, and replaces At 9' by a 'simplified' variant, At 9''.

Purpose. To find axioms under which the global position relations (disjointness, compatibility/transversality) between figures are determined by their atoms (lieux). This is a 'local-to-global by atoms' principle for an abstract tame topology.
errors: In Corollary 1 the quantifier is written over omb(X), omb(Y) while the statement is about figures F, G (notational slip, visible in the image).
Necessity in Corollary 1 is not given by At 9 alone. It needs heredity of ∥ (subfigures of disjoint figures are disjoint), presumably an earlier axiom.
Reducing Corollary 1 to omb(F)∩omb(G)=∅ via Atens 2 tacitly needs lieux to be nonempty (x ∦ x).

In At 9' the transcription's 'x ∦ y (donc x≠y)' is inconsistent: 'donc x≠y' and the bracket omb(X)∩omb(Y)=omb(F) only follow if the hypothesis is x ∥ y (disjoint). The stroke in the image is most plausibly ∥ written heavily.

ideas.what: Disjointness of figures detected on atoms (lieux): F ∥ G iff all their lieux are pairwise disjoint; in the set-theoretic case iff the shadows are disjoint
ideas.modern_name: atomistic lattice / separation by points; disjointness in a contact or mereotopological algebra determined by atoms
ideas.usually_credited_to: lattice theory (Birkhoff); mereotopology (Whitehead, de Vries, later Dimov–Vakarelov contact algebras)
ideas.where_published: Only the unpublished Analysis situs notes; Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 announces tame topology but gives no such axiomatics

ideas.what: Optional axiom At 9': if the lieux of X and Y outside their intersection F are pairwise disjoint (equivalently omb(X)∩omb(Y)=omb(F)), then X ⋔ Y (good/compatible position); converse via a later 'axiome de disposition'
ideas.modern_name: clean intersection / compatibility of cells or strata (regular cell complexes, face posets, frontier condition in stratifications)
ideas.usually_credited_to: stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather); regular CW complexes; o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn)

ideas.what: Idea of encoding the whole atlas (M, ≤, ≪, ≭) set-theoretically through the single relation ≭ on lieux, abandoned because it fails in the important examples (next page)
ideas.modern_name: reconstruction of a space or complex from an incidence relation on atoms (Alexandrov/finite-space or face-poset reconstruction)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (finite spaces), Björner (face posets of regular CW complexes)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatics of figures with a disjointness relation ∥, atoms 'lieux' and a compatibility relation ⋔ is essentially an independent development of a mereotopology / contact-algebra style point-free geometry, aimed at tame topology. This link (Grothendieck's analysis situs ↔ region-based theories of space) is not made in the literature.
missed.quote: Si F, G sont deux figures, pour que F ∥ G, il faut et il suffit que ∀x∈omb(X), y∈omb(Y), on ait x∥y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give an axiomatic, point-free foundation for o-minimal / tame topology. The atoms-detect-disjointness and clean-intersection axioms are exactly what such theories add to Boolean contact algebras.

missed.claim: At 9' is labelled 'facultatif', and its converse is deferred to an 'axiome de disposition'. Which atlases (semialgebraic, PL, subanalytic) satisfy At 9', and its replacement At 9'', is not settled.
missed.quote: At 9' ... Alors X ⋔ Y ... NB La réciproque serait vraie aussi par axiome de disposition plus bas p.72
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete test question for whether Grothendieck's axioms capture o-minimal structures. It is minor but checkable.

deep.surprise_reason: This is internal bookkeeping of an unpublished axiomatic system: a corollary plus an optional axiom on atom-detected disjointness and compatible position. It is of interest as documentation of the 1986 tame-topology programme, but the mathematical content is elementary and close to standard lattice- and stratification-theoretic facts.
transcription_corrections: The opening '[?] [?]' after 'Pour une' is most likely 'Pour un atlas ensembliste' or 'catégorie ensembliste'; the word 'ensembliste' is clearly legible.
'Dans le cas des [?] quelconques, on trouve [?] [?] part' plausibly reads 'Dans le cas des atlas quelconques, on trouve d'autre part.' (uncertain).
In At 9' the relation between x and y is most plausibly x ∥ y (disjoint), not x ∦ y, given 'donc x≠y' and the consequence omb(X)∩omb(Y)=omb(F).
Line 'je voudrais un présenter un axiome' is likely 'je voudrais encore présenter un axiome facultatif'.
The last lines likely read 'Cet axiome est intéressant, en ce qu'il exprime une compatibilité ⋔ des multistructures primitives (qui est une des ...)'.
